targets.summary: Use a DeviceGuard (RAII) here instead of switching the device manually, so the previous device is restored. The same applies at line 332.
targets.adoption_evidence: Before (in the event-creation function, lines 305-309): `C10_CUDA_CHECK(c10::cuda::SetDevice(device_index));`, with a manual GetDevice call and a make_scope_exit restore. After the merge, that whole block is gone and in its place is `c10::impl::InlineDeviceGuard<CUDAGuardImpl> guard(device_index);`, which is an RAII device guard. The diff also adds the `InlineDeviceGuard.h` include. The same swap was made at the IPC handle site (old line 332) and at the other manual device switches in the file.
targets.stage3_reason: The PR hand-rolls device save/restore (`GetDevice(&orig_device); SetDevice(device_index); make_scope_exit(... MaybeSetDevice(orig_device))`) in six places, even though c10 already has an RAII device guard for exactly this. That makes it a real duplication/design problem, not a style nit. The merged code swaps every instance for `c10::impl::InlineDeviceGuard<CUDAGuardImpl> guard(device_index);`, and anyone who knows the c10 guard utilities could flag it from the code alone.
